parts.premise:
Bakari Haynes, an assistant principal with Montgomery County Public Schools in Maryland, says homework completion has improved since students returned to in-person learning. He says teacher and parent interaction helped.

“With virtual learning, it was a struggle for students to log in to their devices and participate,” he says. “With in-person learning, there's more of a connection and push to get students to take homework seriously.”
parts.hypothesis: First graders were doing 28 minutes of homework.
